messages.subject: GGIR Snips off start of epochvalues2csv output
parts:
Hi all,
I come to you with what I assume might be an easy fix.

I have raw acceleration file start:

timestamp accx accy accz
4/04/2009 9:38 -0.307058824 0.794117647 0.518823529
4/04/2009 9:38 -0.307058824 0.794117647 0.518823529
4/04/2009 9:38 -0.307058824 0.794117647 0.518823529
4/04/2009 9:38 -0.307058824 0.794117647 0.518823529
4/04/2009 9:38 -0.307058824 0.794117647 0.518823529
4/04/2009 9:38 -0.307058824 0.794117647 0.518823529

Following processing and specifically, the epochvalues2csv 'function' the start of the csv output is:

timestamp anglex angley anglez ENMO MAD
2009-04-04T13:00:00+0300 4.2991 69.545 19.8921 0 0.0064
2009-04-04T13:00:01+0300 2.6616 71.4474 18.3018 2.00E-04 0.0105
2009-04-04T13:00:02+0300 0.6546 73.1128 16.8408 0.0019 0.0112
2009-04-04T13:00:03+0300 -0.4013 73.2603 16.7278 4.00E-04 0.0037
2009-04-04T13:00:04+0300 -0.1872 73.2119 16.7737 0.001 0.0077
2009-04-04T13:00:05+0300 0.0126 73.8676 16.1135 0.0013 0.0095

Adjusting for the timezone this puts the raw file at start = 9:38AM and the GGIR.csv at start = 10:00AM. GGIR uniformly generates each ID and csv to start at the nearest complete hour. Is there a way to prevent this clipping and to start closer to 9:38AM?

Cheers,

Christian

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: GGIR Snips off start of epochvalues2csv output
parts:
Hi Christian,

You may want to wait for Vincent/Jairo to confirm this, but I'm pretty sure the epochs start on the hour due to your windowsizes argument of 60 minutes for non-wear detection. Because of this I believe GGIR will round the data to the hour so the analysis is neat and easier to summarise variables over the day etc.
As for a solution, I'm not sure what you could do within GGIR, so the solution may be to calculate ENMO on the raw data yourself and adjust based on the calibration output from GGIR. 

Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: GGIR Snips off start of epochvalues2csv output
parts:
Hi Christian and Ben,

Epochs do not start on the hour. They are aligned with the nearest start of a long epoch  which in turn are align with the hour. The long epoch length is by default is 15 minutes. 13:12 becomes 13:15 and 13:27 becomes 13:30, etc.

This is done intentional to standardise epoch alignment relative to the day across individuals and across days. Aligning it with the start of a recording would not be logical.

Note that this has been discussed previously: https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/qUU4-fQmhxw/m/K6MMO3cYAwAJ and in various other threads.

So, to get a resolution closer to the start of the recording you could set windowsizes to c(5, 60, 3600), the second value of which defines the epoch length in seconds.

Also see this recent thread where I explained that the exporting to csv is in itself a redundant functionality as all info is also stored in the RData file.

Thanks,

Vincent
